responses.tool-purpose: Creates differentiated reading resources and follow-up tasks from source text.
responses.problem-solved: It reduces the time needed to adapt academic reading for mixed-ability learners.
responses.feature-interest: Generating levelled versions of the same reading with quick comprehension checks.
responses.test-request: We asked Diffit to adapt a short reading on constructive alignment into multiple learner-friendly versions.
responses.test-what-happened: It generated simpler text versions, glossary support, and several starter questions that were usable with edits.
responses.surprised: The vocabulary support was stronger than the discussion prompts.
responses.corrected: We rewrote two generic questions and checked one summary where nuance had been reduced too far.

strengths.text: Quickly differentiates reading material for mixed-ability groups.
Provides useful glossary and starter questions.

weaknesses.text: Some outputs become too generic without teacher editing.

opportunities.text: Could support pre-seminar access tasks for students with lower confidence.

threats.text: Teachers may trust simplified explanations that remove important detail.

responses.learning-improve: It could improve access to difficult readings by lowering the initial comprehension barrier.
responses.teacher-time: Preparing differentiated reading packs and first-draft questions.
responses.strongest-use: Producing accessible pre-class reading tasks quickly.
responses.avoid-use: Avoid it when original disciplinary wording is central to the learning outcome.
responses.check-before-use: Check the accuracy of summaries and whether the simplification keeps the intended meaning.

quadrant-map.rationale: It saves substantial preparation time with moderate risk if outputs are reviewed carefully.

responses.ai-decisions: It decided what to simplify, what vocabulary to foreground, and how to frame starter questions.
responses.human-judgement-needed: An educator must judge whether simplification preserves conceptual accuracy and appropriate challenge.
responses.concerned: An inexperienced educator could accept the generated text without noticing where the meaning was flattened.
responses.other-educators-know: It works best as a drafting and adaptation tool, not a finished classroom resource.
responses.view-change: We expected a basic worksheet generator, but it felt more valuable as a differentiation support tool.
